title: Nests along the Hedge
story: The science club counted bird nests in the school grounds on a dry morning. They stayed on the path and used binoculars. The rule was clear to everyone. They could look and record, but they could not touch. In the oak they found two nests high above the path. In the long hedge they found four more. A student named Ruth marked each nest on a simple map. She used a circle for the oak and a square for the hedge. Nobody climbed, and nobody used a stick. The teacher praised the group for leaving the birds in peace. They stored the map in a folder in the lab. The plan was to return in spring and see which nests were busy. Ruth copied the map into her notebook that evening. She added the date and the weather at the top. The club hoped the same birds would come back.
